title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — 2026 (Comprehensive, v40)
author: Evan Martinez
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response practices, runbook templates, postmortem expectations, rotation rules, game day guidance, and customer/status communication templates. It is intended for engineers, SREs, support, and product owners who participate in incident response and post-incident improvement work.

Scope:
- Applies to all production-facing services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Private deployments control plane).
- Includes guidance for severity classification, triage, mitigation, stakeholder communications, and retrospective actions.

Goals:
- Restore customer-facing service within defined SLOs while minimizing user impact.
- Provide clear ownership, fast decision making, and consistent communications.
- Capture learnings to prevent recurrence and reduce mean time to repair (MTTR).

Definitions and Severity Levels:
1) Sev 1 (Critical): Service-wide outage or large-scale data loss (e.g., API returns 5xx for >10% of requests across regions, total inability to serve model inference for >=5 minutes). Requires immediate page, conference bridge, and executive notification.
2) Sev 2 (High): Significant degradation (e.g., sustained latency > 2x P90 SLA for a major route, or a single region degraded affecting >5% traffic). Page on-call and notify product and support.
3) Sev 3 (Medium): Partial degradation or feature breakage with limited customer impact (e.g., embeddings throughput reduced for non-critical tenants). Handled during business hours or by on-call if needed.
4) Sev 4 (Low): Non-urgent issues, scheduled fixes, or ops tasks. Track as tickets; do not page.

Incident Lifecycle (high level):
1. Detection: Alert triggers, customer report, or internal observation.
2. Triage (first 10 minutes): Identify scope, impacted services/customers, and severity. Assign a lead.
3. Mitigation: Apply short-term mitigations to restore user-facing functionality.
4. Communicate: Open an incident page, notify stakeholders, and update the status page.
5. Stabilize: Confirm service is functioning and monitor for reoccurrence.
6. Postmortem: Write a blameless postmortem within 72 hours for Sev1/2; include action items.
7. Follow-up: Implement and track corrective actions to completion.

Triage Checklist (first 10 minutes):
- Acknowledge the page and mark ownership in the incident channel.
- Capture initial facts: time detected, source of detection, last deploys, traffic/heatmaps.
- Identify whether to escalate to Sev1/Sev2 process.
- If Sev1: start conference bridge (Zoom/Jitsi), page senior SRE/engineering manager, and notify on-call support lead.
- If customer-facing: create status page incident and a short customer-facing summary.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): Owns overall incident coordination, decisions, and communications.
- Primary On-call: First responder; executes runbooks and mitigations.
- Secondary On-call: Backup; takes over if primary unavailable.
- Service Owner: Provides deep domain knowledge, approves rollbacks or risky changes.
- Communications Lead: Writes and updates status page and customer comms.
- Scribe: Records actions and timeline in the incident document.

Escalation Matrix (example):
- Primary on-call (0-10 min) -> Secondary on-call (10-20 min) -> Senior SRE (20-30 min) -> Engineering Manager -> Head of Infrastructure.

Runbook Templates and Examples:
(Each runbook should include: purpose, detection signals, pre-reqs, step-by-step mitigation, verification, rollback, and owner.)

Runbook: API request latency spike (service: redwood-api/gateway)
- Purpose: Mitigate sudden high latency for realtime text generation routes.
- Detection signals: P95 latency > 1.5s for >5 minutes; alert: api.latency.p95.alert.
- Pre-reqs: PagerDuty runbook access, Grafana + Tempo, deployment tags.
Steps:
  1) Acknowledge alert and assign IC.
  2) Check recent deploys: `git log --oneline --since=1h` and deployment dashboard.
  3) Confirm whether the issue is regional: inspect region-filtered QPS and error rates.
  4) If errors increased (5xx): check upstream model-serving pool health (gpu-pool-*), restart unhealthy pods (`kubectl rollout restart deployment/<service> -n prod`) only after approval from Service Owner.
  5) If latency-only and CPU/GPU utilization is high: scale up autoscaling group or increase concurrency limit for impacted nodes (see infra runbook).
  6) If cache miss rate spiked: enable prefix caching warmup or revert recent cache invalidations.
  7) Verify mitigation: watch P95/P99 for 10 minutes; if still degrading, consider traffic routing to standby region or fallback model variant.
  8) Communicate: update incident doc and status page every 15 minutes until stabilized.

Runbook: GPU pool degraded (service: inference-gpu-pool)
- Purpose: Restore capacity when a GPU node pool experiences instance failures or driver-level faults.
- Detection signals: gpu.node.failures.rate > 0.5% per minute OR job queue length growing > 3x.
Steps:
  1) Confirm provider incident (check cloud provider status).
  2) Drain problematic nodes: `kubectl cordon <node>` and `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets`.
  3) Replace nodes via autoscaling group / machine pool (see cloud-accounts-and-networking runbook).
  4) If driver crash (nvidia): collect dmesg and logs, escalate to infra with tag `gpu-driver` and consider kernel/drivers rollback if changed in last 24h.
  5) If capacity cannot be restored quickly: route new requests to Dedicated spare capacity / fallback region and enable rate limit relaxations for enterprise customers per SLA policy.
  6) Verify by monitoring GPU utilization and queue length; confirm back to normal for 30 minutes before closing incident.

Postmortem Template (use for all Sev1/2 incidents):
- Title (one line)
- Incident ID
- Timeline (ISO timestamps with short bullets)
- Summary (what happened, impact, duration)
- Contributing factors (root causes and contributing issues)
- Detection and response (what we did and when)
- Customer impact (customers affected, support tickets opened)
- Corrective actions (owner, due date, status)
- Preventative actions (longer-term work)
- Follow-ups and monitoring plan
- Links: incident doc, runbooks, dashboards, relevant PRs.

Postmortem expectations:
- Postmortem must be filed within 72 hours for Sev1/2; all action items must have an owner and reasonable due date.
- At 30/60/90 day intervals, owners must report status on action items in the incident backlog until completion.
- Severity should be reassessed postmortem; if repeat incidents observed, escalate to reliability initiative.

On-call Rotations and Handoff Rules:
- Rotation cadence: 1 week primary on-call per engineer; 2-week cycle for secondary. Weekend on-call is covered by primary with manager backup.
- Shift responsibilities: Primary handles pages during their week; Secondary provides daytime backup and takes over for extended incidents.
- Handoff checklist (to be completed in Slack on rotation change):
  - Confirm runbook access and PagerDuty/Slack channels.
  - Share any ongoing incidents or escalations.
  - List expected maintenance or deployments during the coming week.
  - Confirm contact info and escalation path.
- Vacation & swap policy: Engineers must publish swap at least 72 hours in advance and ensure replacements are onboarded with runbooks.

Game Days (purpose and sample plan):
- Purpose: Validate runbooks, improve coordination, and test automation/rollbacks.
- Frequency: Quarterly per major platform area (API, GPU fleet, control plane).
- Participants: On-call engineers, service owners, product (as observer), customer success (for communications), and infra.
- Sample Game Day (2 hours):
  1) Kickoff (10 min): Objectives and scope.
  2) Inject (30 min): Simulated failure (e.g., region network partition, model-serving kernel panic).
  3) Triage & mitigate (40 min): Follow runbook, practice communications.
  4) Retro (30 min): Capture observations, assign improvements.
  5) Close (10 min): Summarize action items.
- Deliverables: updated runbooks, action items with owners, and a short game day report posted to the incident playbook.

Status Page & Customer Communications Templates:
- Status page cadence: initial post within 10 minutes of detection for Sev1/Sev2; updates every 15 minutes for ongoing incidents until mitigation; final update when incident is fully resolved with root cause summary (can be delayed until postmortem).

Status page template (short):
- Title: [Incident] {short summary} (Region/Service)
- Impact: {e.g., Partial outage to hosted API in us-west-2} 
- Status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Resolved
- Started: {ISO timestamp}
- Updated: {ISO timestamp}
- Next update: {relative time}
- Details: short plain-language description and recommended workarounds.
- Affected Customers: {if known; otherwise: unknown} 

Customer-facing email template (severe incident initial):
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood Inference {service} — {region} — {short time}
Body:
Hello,

We are experiencing an issue affecting {service} in {region}. Our engineering team is actively investigating. We will provide updates every 15 minutes. We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a full incident report once the root cause is determined.

If you have critical business impact, please reply to this message or contact support@redwood.ai with your account ID and a brief description.

— Redwood Inference Reliability Team

Internal comms snippets (slack/status channel):
- Initial: `INCIDENT: {service} {region} — Impact: {summary} — Assigned: @{oncall} — IC: @{ic}`
- Update: `INCIDENT UPDATE: {service} — {short update} — Next update in 15m`
- Resolved: `RESOLVED: {service} — Incident ended at {time} — Postmortem to follow`

Metrics, Alerts, and SLOs (examples):
- API generation route (text.generate): SLO: 99.9% success within 1.0s P95 monthly.
- Alerts:
  - api.errors.rate > 0.5% for 5m -> Sev2 alert
  - api.latency.p95 > 1.5s for 5m -> Sev2 alert
  - gpu.node.failures.rate > 0.5% per minute -> Sev1 alert
- Monitoring: Grafana dashboards (API Overview, GPU Fleet Health, KV Cache Hit Rate), distributed traces in Tempo, logs in Loki.

Ownership and Contacts (primary contacts by area):
- API & Gateway: ownership: eng-platform (oncall channel #oncall-api, owners: Eng Platform team leads)
- Serving runtime & GPU pools: eng-serving-runtime (#oncall-serving-runtime)
- Infra / Cloud accounts: eng-infra (#oncall-infra)
- Customer communications & escalations: customer-success (#support)

Incident Documentation and Tooling:
- Every incident must have an incident doc (confluence/incident/{incident-id}) with timeline and notes.
- Use PagerDuty for paging and Zoom/Jitsi for bridges.
- Link monitoring, runbooks, and PRs in the incident doc.

Post-incident Follow-up Process:
1) Assign action items in the postmortem with owners and due dates.
2) Add higher-priority items to the Reliability Initiatives board if they require cross-team work.
3) Check closed-loop: verify that fixes are deployed and monitoring alarms updated.
4) Report summary at monthly Reliability review meeting.

Appendix: Example Incident Timeline (short)
- 2026-01-22T14:07Z — Alert: api.latency.p95.alert triggered.
- 2026-01-22T14:09Z — Primary on-call acknowledges, IC assigned.
- 2026-01-22T14:15Z — Identified region us-west-2, recent deploy at 13:50Z.
- 2026-01-22T14:25Z — Rolled back deployment; latency restored to baseline at 14:33Z.
- 2026-01-22T15:10Z — Incident declared resolved. Postmortem assigned to service owner.
